title: Firefighter pay contract arbitration and mediation
summary: A union representative told the Fire and Public Safety Commission that firefighters take 28 years to reach top pay and the applicant pool is down 73%, and the fire chief said contract talks went to arbitration with a decision on April 1, while the union said the dispute is now in mediation. The commission added the salary issue to its next agenda, and the Civil Service Commission heard that corporation counsel will take added fire contract costs to the County Council for approval.

timeline.text: Corporation counsel will take added fire contract costs to the County Council for approval.
Motion to add the salary negotiation and arbitration items discussed to the next meeting's agenda: The motion passed by roll call vote.
The next meeting will include an update on the arbitration process and the testifier's handouts.
The chair asked corporation counsel (the County's lawyers) to explain at the next meeting what the commission can and cannot do on the salary issue.
The union representative said the dispute is now in mediation.
The arbitrator's written decision came on April 1.
The fire chief said contract talks reached an impasse and went to arbitration, where an outside person decides.
The union representative said a supplemental agreement could include housing incentives for firefighters.
A union representative said applicants cannot afford a pay cut and still live where they grew up.
A union representative testified that firefighters take 28 years to reach top pay.
A fire department official said firefighter contract arbitration ended in early April but is still being finalized.
A union representative testified that Maui Fire Department pay is under the 40th percentile when cost-of-living changes are added.
